'''Trevor Fitzgerald Booker''' (born November 25, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted 23rd overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]], but was immediately traded to the [[Washington Wizards]]. Booker primarily played the [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.

==Early life==
Booker was born on November 25, 1987, in [[Newberry, South Carolina]], to Gerald and Tracey, both accomplished athletes. He was brought up in a rural [[Whitmire, South Carolina|Whitmire]] neighborhood and grew up eating as many as 20 bowls of [[breakfast cereal|cereal]] each week, sharing the love with his brothers.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Steinberg|first1=Dan|title=Trevor Booker leaves Wizards with final cereal interview|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/dc-sports-bog/wp/2014/07/15/trevor-booker-leaves-wizards-with-final-cereal-interview/|website=WashingtonPost.com|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref> Booker began playing the game of basketball after his mother tried to get her sons into it by showing them her highlights as a high school player. His brother, [[Devin Booker (basketball, born 1991)|Devin]], said, "She got us into it when we were younger, and we have been ever since."<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cobbs|first1=Matt|title=Booker brothers synonymous with Union County basketball|url=http://www.goupstate.com/article/20080314/NEWS/7419702?tc=ar|website=GoUpstate.com|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref>

==High school career==
Booker attended Union High School in [[Union, South Carolina]], and played basketball under head coach Joe Pitt. In his senior year in 2005–06, Booker was named [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for [[South Carolina]], after averaging 21.9 points, 16.4 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game. He was also named AAA State Player of the Year and was a first-time All-State selection. Booker left the Union high school team as its all-time leader in rebounds and blocked shots. Later on, Booker played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball with the South Carolina Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker to Receive Key to the City of Mauldin, SC|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=205505409|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman===
Entering college, Booker was listed as a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and [[247Sports.com]]. He was ranked the 29th best [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] by Rivals and 27th by 247Sports in the Class of 2006. Booker was also given a 0.8778 composite rating at 247Sports.com.<ref name="Trevor Booker">{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Trevor-Booker-37973|website=Rivals.com|access-date=26 December 2014}}</ref><ref name=union>{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker at Union|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Trevor-Booker-64667/?Institution=20023|website=247Sports.com|access-date=26 December 2014}}</ref> He committed to play for the [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball]] team on May 13, 2005, officially visited [[Clemson University|Clemson]] on September 16, 2005, signed the [[National Letter of Intent]] with Clemson on February 1, 2006, and enrolled on May 30, 2006.<ref name="union" /> Booker also considered [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]], [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]], and [[Wofford Terriers men's basketball|Wofford]] as possible destinations. He received offers from Wofford, William & Mary, and South Carolina.<ref name="Trevor Booker"/>

On October 31, 2006, Booker made his collegiate debut with [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], recording six points, seven rebounds, three blocks, and three steals as starting [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in an exhibition game against [[Lithuanian Sports University|Lithuania Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Clemson Downs Lithuania Academy 99–50|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205508185&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> He was allowed 18 minutes on the court, and along with Sam Perry, led the team in rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lithuania Academy vs Clemson (10/31/06 at Clemson, SC (Littlejohn Coliseum)|url=http://www.nmnathletics.com/ViewContent.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&CONTENT_ID=208087|website=NMNAthletics.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> Booker made his first regular season appearance with the Tigers on November 10, 2006, in the first round of the Cox Communications Classic against [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State]]. After starting as [[center (basketball)|center]], he became the first true freshman to start in that position for Clemson since Tom Wideman in 1995–96. He finished the game with 6 points, a team-high 7 rebounds, and 1 block in 19 minutes of playing time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Clemson Downs Arkansas State, 83–44, in Season Opener|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205524916&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref><ref name=realgm>{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Trevor-Booker/GameLogs/3685/NCAA/2007|website=RealGM.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> On November 12, 2006, Booker grabbed a career-best 9 rebounds vs [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion]] for the Cox Communications Classic title. He also contributed 10 points.<ref name="realgm" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Clemson Tops ODU For Cox Communications Classic Title|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205508416&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> On November 17, 2006, Booker scored a career-high 15 points in 20 minutes against [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]].<ref name="realgm" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Tigers Improve To 5–0 With 79–49 Rout Of Mountaineers|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205512592&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> Booker recorded 11 rebounds on November 24 of the same year in a win over [[Charleston Southern Buccaneers men's basketball|Charleston Southern]]. It was his first collegiate game with 10+ boards.<ref name="realgm" /> On December 31, 2006, he recorded his first career double-double, with 15 points and 12 rebounds on [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State]]. [[James Mays (basketball)|James Mays]], one of his teammates, when asked about Booker's accomplishments, said, "What didn't he do?" Booker helped Clemson reach 14–0, their best start in 20 years.<ref name="realgm" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Tigers Reach 14–0 With 67–57 Victory Over Georgia State|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205522755&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> On January 6, 2007, Booker had [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] freshman [[Zach Peacock]] ejected from the game after he hit him with an elbow.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mays' Layup Sends No. 23 Tigers To Victory Over Yellow Jackets, 75–74|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205510418&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> On March 19, 2007, Booker scored a career-high 21 points against [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Booker, Hammonds Lead Clemson Rout Over Ole Miss, 89–68, In NIT Second Round|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205515068&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref> By the end of his freshman season, Booker averaged 10.4 points, a team-high 6.7 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks. He ranked fourth nationally among freshmen in shots blocked.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker – Basketball Player Profile|url=http://www.tigernet.com/clemson-basketball/player/Trevor-Booker-14|website=TigerNet.com|access-date=25 December 2014}}</ref>

===Sophomore and Junior===
In his sophomore and junior seasons, Clemson had its first back-to-back NCAA appearances in nearly ten years. In Booker's junior year he led the ACC in rebounding (9.7 per game) and field goal percentage (.571), and finished second in blocked shots (2.0 per game).<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120304043454/http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040709aaa.html|title=Booker Led ACC in Rebounding and Field Goal Percentage}}</ref> For his efforts, Booker was named second-team All-ACC and was named to the 2009 All-Defensive Team.<ref>[http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030909aaa.html Booker Named to Second-Team All-ACC & ACC's All-Defensive Team] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312060903/http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030909aaa.html |date=2009-03-12 }}</ref> On the National level, he was named [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] All-District<ref>[https://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2009/alldistrict090310.html USBWA NAMES 2008–09 MEN'S ALL-DISTRICT TEAMS]</ref> and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] second team All-District.<ref>[http://www.nabc.org/genrel/030409aaa.html NABC Announces 2009 Division I All-District Teams]</ref> Following his junior year, Booker announced that he would return to Clemson for his senior year.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4022000 Booker will return to Clemson]</ref> He spent the summer following his junior campaign playing for Team USA in the [[World University Games]], helping the team win a bronze medal.

===Senior===
During his senior year, Booker was selected the All-ACC first team.<ref>[http://www.tigernet.com/view/story.do?id=8458 Trevor Booker Named First-Team All-ACC]</ref>

==Professional career==

===Washington Wizards (2010–2014)===
[[File:Trevor Booker 2011.jpg|thumb|right|Booker in 2011]]
Booker was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 23rd overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] on draft night.

On August 4, 2011, Booker signed with [[Bnei Herzliya|Bnei Hasharon]] of Israel for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/87848/bnei-hasharon-adds-size-with-trevor-booker.html Bnei Hasharon adds size with Trevor Booker]</ref> In October 2011, he returned to the United States due to a bruised right quadriceps.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/88726/jj-hickson-agreed-to-terms-with-bnei-hasharon.html JJ Hickson agreed to terms with Bnei Hasharon]</ref> In December 2011, following the conclusion of the lockout, Booker returned to the Washington Wizards before appearing in a game for Bnei Hasharon.

===Utah Jazz (2014–2016)===
On July 21, 2014, Booker signed with the [[Utah Jazz]]<ref>[https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-free-agent-trevor-booker Jazz Signs Free Agent Trevor Booker]</ref> to a reported two-year, $10 million contract.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234309/Trevor-Booker-Agrees-To-Two-Year-$10M-Deal-With-Jazz Trevor Booker Agrees To Two-Year, $10M Deal With Jazz]</ref> On April 11, 2015, Booker scored a career-high 36 points in a win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150414004947/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865626256/Trevor-Bookers-36-points-2-a-career-high-2-lift-the-Utah-Jazz.html Trevor Booker's career-high 36 points power Jazz past Blazers]</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2016–2017)===
On July 8, 2016, Booker signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/07/08/brooklyn-nets-sign-trevor-booker|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Trevor Booker|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> On December 14, he grabbed a season-high 18 rebounds in a 107–97 win over the [[2016–17 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899820|title=Nets send Lakers to 8th straight loss, 107–97|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref> On April 1, 2017, Booker scored a season-high 23 points in a 121–111 win over the [[2016–17 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899396|title=Lopez leads Nets over Magic, 121–111|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2017|access-date=April 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2017–2018)===
On December 7, 2017, Booker was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Jahlil Okafor]], [[Nik Stauskas]], and a 2019 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/76ers-acquire-trevor-booker-brooklyn|title=76ers Acquire Trevor Booker From Brooklyn|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=December 7, 2017}}</ref> On February 28, 2018, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-sign-forward-ersan-ilyasova|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Forward Ersan Ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2018|access-date=February 28, 2018}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2018)===
On March 3, 2018, Booker signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-trevor-booker|title=Pacers Sign Trevor Booker|work=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2018|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Trevor Booker (25998898157).jpg|thumb|right|Booker with the Pacers in March 2018]]

In August 2018, Booker signed a one-year contract to play with the [[Shanxi Brave Dragons]] in the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/nba-free-agency-news-trevor-booker-signing-china-utah-jazz-pacers-contract-shanxi-brave-dragons/zhxi6orea3zy1323x3xeuskgv |title=NBA free agency news: Trevor Booker signs 1-year deal with China's Shanxi Brave Dragons {{!}} NBA {{!}} Sporting News |website=www.sportingnews.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809150415/http://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/nba-free-agency-news-trevor-booker-signing-china-utah-jazz-pacers-contract-shanxi-brave-dragons/zhxi6orea3zy1323x3xeuskgv |archive-date=2018-08-09}}</ref> On October 11, 2018, Booker returned to the United States to have surgery performed on his foot.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trevor Booker: To undergo foot surgery|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trevor-booker-to-undergo-foot-surgery/|website=CBS Sports|access-date=February 20, 2019|date=October 11, 2018}}</ref>

On April 14, 2020, Booker announced his retirement from his basketball career at age 32.<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 14, 2020|title=Former Wizards forward Trevor Booker announces retiremen after eight seasons|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/former-wizards-forward-trevor-booker-announces-retirement-after-eight-seasons|website=NBC Sports Washington}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Coles|first=Joe|date=April 15, 2020|title=Former Jazz forward Trevor Booker retires from the NBA|language=en|work=[[Deseret News]]|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/4/15/21221748/trevor-booker-former-jazz-forward-retires-nba|access-date=April 20, 2020}}</ref>

Booker started working out with the minor league [[PrimeTime Players]] of the [[East Coast Basketball League]] and [[The Basketball Tournament|The Tournament]] fame. He made his ECBL debut on March 6, 2021, scoring 36 points and 18 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 6, 2021|title=Carolina Crusaders vs. PrimeTime Players|url=https://www.primetimeplayersbasketball.com/teams/default.asp?u=PRIMETIMEPLAYERS&s=basketball&sportsHQ=PRIMETIMEPLAYERS&gameID=2137976&p=boxscore|website=PrimeTime Players}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Booker has three younger brothers; [[Devin Booker (basketball, born 1991)|Devin]], Darrion, and Jared.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Devin Booker: basketball is mostly a family matter|url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/devin-booker-basketball-is-mostly-a-family-matter/|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=olimpiamilano.com|language=en}}</ref> Devin also played college basketball for Clemson University and now plays professionally in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|title=Devin Booker Bio|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205528964&DB_OEM_ID=28500|website=ClemsonTigers.com|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref> Darrion played college basketball for the [[University of West Alabama]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Darrion Booker Bio|url=http://www.uwaathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=816|website=UWAAthletics.com|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref> and Jared competes with the Union County High School basketball team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jared Booker Profile|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/jared-booker/oI9WclSwEeOzMAAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|publisher=CBS Sports|access-date=23 December 2014}}</ref> Booker is also the cousin of NBA player [[Jordan Hill (basketball)|Jordan Hill]].<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-trevor-booker-still-waiting-to-play-his-cousin-jordan-hill/2012/01/27/gIQAkyzVWQ_blog.html Wizards’ Trevor Booker still waiting to play his cousin, Jordan Hill]</ref>
